newsitem.title: KENYA: LUFTHANSA CANCELS NAIROBI 747F RETURN STOP.
newsitem.headline: LUFTHANSA CANCELS NAIROBI 747F RETURN STOP.

text.p: Lufthansa Cargo has cancelled the return-scheduled stop in Nairobi of a Boeing-747 freighter on its leg from Johannesburg to Frankfurt on Friday amid concerns over a general strike planned by Kenya's opposition.

A Lufthansa official said the aircraft will fly Frankfurt-Nairobi-Johannesburg-Frankfurt, unload some cargo from Frankfurt in Nairobi and load a small amount of Nairobi-Frankfurt bound cargo before heading south.

"It arrives here early Friday morning from Frankfurt and we will load the cargo for Frankfurt then and cancel the second stop in Nairobi. It then flies to Johannesburg and then direct back to Frankfurt, missing out Nairobi.
"We think we can get all the Frankfurt load in with just one stop because most shippers have cancelled due to the national strike so there is much less than normal," the official told Reuters.

David Keary, general manager for East and Central Africa for Lufthansa Cargo, told Reuters earlier this week that he estimated total losses from the cargo load scheduled for Friday to be worth in the region of $400,000.

Keary said on Wednesday that a go-slow which crippled business in all Kenyan airports from last Friday-midnight until midday Thursday combined with calls by Kenya's opposition for a national strike on Friday had caused security concerns.

"I am worried about the safety...if the general strike takes off, usually the first thing which will be hit is the transport sector. The fire brigade, the meteorological department...all the essential requirements needed to handle an operation appears to be in jeopardy.

He then said Friday's cargo shipment was expected to consist of between 60 and 70 tonnes of cut flowers, vegetables and fresh fish for European markets. - Reuters Air Cargo Service Tel+ 44 171 542 7706 Fax +5017 - www.racs.com
